summary: A 1975 list of references and contacts about the various protocols used on the ARPANET, along with recent developments. It updates RFC 661.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 694 is a directory of ARPANET protocol work as of June 1975. It points readers to documents and contacts, and distinguishes protocols marked as official from experimental activity.

questions: where to find arpanet protocol documents
what protocols existed on the arpanet in 1975
who maintained the arpanet protocol information file
subtitle: A directory of ARPANET protocols, documents, contacts and recent developments.

tldr.problem: Protocol information, documents and contacts were spread across many files and publications.
tldr.mechanism: Jon Postel's compendium groups protocol entries with contacts, documents, people, schedules, comments and recent developments, marking official standards.
tldr.outcome: RFC 694 updates RFC 661 and asks readers to provide corrections and new information so the file can be kept current.

today: The unit records RFC 694's status as Unknown and says it updates RFC 661. It is a June 1975 snapshot of a protocol information file that the author intended to keep current.

sections.title: A Maintained Protocol Information File
sections.content:
The file collects information about protocol-related activity on the ARPA Network. It says most of that activity is experimental, and appends “[Official]” to protocols it identifies as official standards. The author asks users to send developments and corrections so the information can be kept current.

The RFC points to online protocol documents, RFC indexes, official host-name information, liaison lists and the NIC's hardcopy RFC library. It also identifies a collection of documents filed with the National Technical Information Service as the more-or-less official protocols as of 1 December 1974.
sections.plainLanguage: The file gathers references and contacts for many protocols in one place. Readers are asked to report changes so the directory can be updated.

sections.title: Network and Host Protocol Entries
sections.content:
The directory covers IMP-IMP, IMP-HOST and Host-Host protocols. It lists contacts and documents and records changes, such as the IMP-HOST message identification field, updates to BBN Report 1822 and proposals for changes to the Host-IMP protocol.

Host-Host entries include the official NCP, experimental reliability-related work and the lost-message detection proposal. The file also lists other efforts such as Message Switching Protocol, TCP, Network Voice Protocol, packet radio, Host-Front End and debugging protocols, with brief status notes where provided.
sections.plainLanguage: The first part covers how network processors and hosts exchange messages. It lists official protocols alongside experiments and proposals, with references to their documents.

sections.title: Telnet, FTP and Mail Information
sections.content:
The Telnet section distinguishes Old and New Telnet and lists the New Telnet options, their option numbers, documents and contacts. It notes a target date for hosts to run the new protocol and refers readers to a survey of servers and a schedule for TIP implementation.

The FTP section lists old and new file transfer, related documents and recent developments including TENEX paged-file support and a proposal to fix FTP-1. The mail section lists current and proposed mail documents and contact information.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory helps readers find the documents and contacts for Telnet, FTP and mail. It also records recent work and proposals for these protocols.

sections.title: Other Protocols and Number Assignments
sections.content:
Later sections cover remote job entry, graphics, the Data Reconfiguration Service, RSEXEC, the Line Processor Protocol, NETED and the Unified User-Level Protocol. A section on the National Software Works lists its distributed programming documents and notes that the documents describe an earlier state and may not reflect later implementation details.

The final material includes assigned links and sockets, their uses, contacts and recent assignments. These tables are part of the information file's role as a practical index to network protocol work.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory also covers services, projects and assigned network numbers. It cautions that some National Software Works documents describe an earlier design rather than current implementation details.
